Your idea is sound- for the purposes of being aggregated or appearing on "all", unpopular subforums should have a really hard time to have a post pop to the top.

To show why the current system is broken, it goes like this:

Pretend that instead of a text preview (the title), each post was an image, like on an imageboard. Now pretend that there was a devoted but small group of people who exchanged some image you find disturbing, or something you wouldn't like showing up if you went to browse "all". Assume that this picture set was universally blocked by many users who did not want to see it. Neither did they want to go to the forum for any purpose, downvoting included- they want to leave them alone to their sick ass pictures.

The current algo would result in a lot of those pictures showing up on "all", because a decent number of users would simply be ignoring it. They don't want to go and brigade or otherwise harass, they just want to ignore. But by doing so, the pictures show up on an aggregate page, despite their unpopularity- unpopularity not expressed with "downvotes", but by simply opting out of interaction.

The more people opt out of a sub, the less likely it should be to show up in an aggregate place, because it means that the sub is not very indicative of the user base- it's simply something that people aren't trying to fight or fuck with, they just don't want to see it.

I do agree that you might have to factor in how much the "blocking" account is actually used- you wouldn't want someone to be able to "block brigade" trivially with fake accounts, or at least, this should be about as hard as vote brigading.

So do you want an assembled AR-15? Or are you wanting to stick with a bolt action? Cause there really aren't many 5.56mm semi autos that aren't AR-15s and cheap. Also AR-15s get just as dirty as any other gun. I personally find it relaxing to break it down and clean it. A quick clean can be done in 5 minutes or a detailed clean in 30 mins.
Maybe look into old 7.62X39 guns. Like the SKS, Or the CZ 858 if you want something a little more modern.

You'll eventually end up with an AR, so might as well just grab a $500 one, and you can customize it later. You could get a Mini14, but ARs are the Barbie doll of rifles...just so many ways to dress them!;) Resale value will hold up pretty well too, since the market is so huge.

I just built myself a AR-15 from Palmetto State Armory by buying a fully assembled blemished lower and a 16" upper assembly with bolt carrier group and charging handle. then I ordered a carry handle/rear sight on Cheaper Than Dirt. $460 all said and done. $500 with the magazines I picked up locally.

All I had to do to assemble this was pop in two pins to join the upper to the lower, tighten two screws and function-check everything. (there are free pdfs for AR-15 manuals online).

Took it out to the range, and barely had to tune the sights. Shot really, REALLY well.

Honestly, the hardest part about building it was "waiting for it to ship"

Re. Del-Ton, are you sure you want a classic front sight with a flat-top? You'd need to put optics on raisers. It may be a good idea, depending on your body build and shooting habits, but it does look a bit unusual. The contemporary style is to build with a monolithic upper and put flip-ups if you feel that you need backups.
Cheap and good don't often cross paths where guns are concerned, but go with the Ruger over the Kel Tec for sure.

Loads of great suggestions here. We're in a golden era of gun manufacturing where there are many options for affordable AR-15 platform rifles. I would go with a milspec AR build from a reputable manufacturer - ie Colt, Bushmaster, Stag, Spikes,etc.. On the cheaper end you can find Smith & Wesson or DPMS options very cheap. Just be careful that if you buy used that you don't end up with someone's project gone awry. I would stick with a factory build so you'll know it works. Then you can either upgrade it or start building your second one one piece at a time.
